subject: Recap: Private deployment discovery — data paths, logging & on‑prem constraints (AtlasHealth)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@atlashealth.com>, IT Ops <itops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Private deployment discovery — data paths, logging & on‑prem constraints (AtlasHealth)

Hi Samantha / Atlas IT team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and open asks so we have alignment for the pilot next week. I pasted the main notes below (oldest -> newest).

Call summary (items you asked us to confirm):
- Scope: Private deployment in your AWS account (VPC) with no general internet egress. Redwood control plane will be managed via private endpoints (we proposed PrivateLink).
- PII types: PHI tokens in payloads + user identifiers (email/mobile). Atlas requirement: PII may not persist in logs in cleartext; pseudonymization preferred on ingest.
- Retention: Primary data retention in Atlas-managed S3 (90 days for full text, 1 year for metadata unless otherwise requested).
- Logging: App logs must be forwardable to your Splunk cluster in the colo; access to raw token-level request logs is restricted. Audit logs (request ID, model version, latency, status) ok to ship.
- Key management: Atlas requires customer-managed keys (KMS + optional HSM) for stored artifacts and wants envelope encryption for any persisted cache.
- Network constraints: No direct outbound to the public internet from inference nodes. Allowed egress: Atlas-approved S3 endpoints and a single proxy host (per your security team).
- Airgap/on‑prem: If we cannot allow the PrivateLink path, we discussed an on‑prem airgapped package (manual upload of model artifacts, no control plane egress) — this will have higher ops overhead and a longer lead time.

Open asks for Atlas (items we need answers to to finalize the pilot design):
1) Can you confirm the exact S3 endpoints (bucket ARNs or regional endpoints) we are authorized to talk to?
2) Will Splunk accept TLS‑over‑private-link ingests, or will you require a Pull aggregator inside the VPC?
3) Do you require request‑level token redaction at the agent layer or is pseudonymization before log forward acceptable?
4) Who is the internal approver for HSM/KMS integration (security contact name/email)?

Attachments: redwood-data-map-v1.pdf (technical sketch we discussed).

Next steps (Redwood):
- Ben will draft architecture options (PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway vs airgap) and a proposed pilot MOP.
- We’ll produce a short ARO (architecture + runbook + ops playbook) for your security review by Friday.

Thanks — can you reply inline with answers to the four open asks and attach any IP ranges or proxy host FQDNs?

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Liu <samantha@atlashealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, IT Ops <itops@atlashealth.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment discovery — data paths, logging & on‑prem constraints (AtlasHealth)

Thanks Aisha — helpful recap. Quick answers below from our security / infra side: we copied IT Ops for specifics.

Answers to your asks:
1) S3 endpoints: Allowed buckets are s3://atlas-prod-logs (us-east-1) and s3://atlas-archive (us-west-2, for long term). We’ll send an IP/CIDR list for the VPC peering proxies separately.
2) Splunk: We prefer a Pull aggregator inside the VPC (our Splunk indexers do not accept public TLS pushes). You can push to the aggregator (TLS) within the peered VPC; the aggregator will do the forward to colo.
3) Logs: Pseudonymization at the agent layer is acceptable. We require that request text tokens classified as PHI be replaced with a stable pseudonym prior to any log forwarding. Audit logs (nontext) may include request IDs, timing, and model metadata.
4) Security approver for KMS/HSM: Mark Rojas (mark.rojas@atlashealth.com), Security Operations lead. He’ll own the KMS integration sign-off.

Constraints / additional notes:
- No outbound internet from inference nodes permitted. Egress must be tightly restricted to approved endpoints and the proxy.
- For an airgap scenario, we will need a signed checklist and a maintenance window for manual artifact uploads. That path will require a higher level of MSA/SoW detail.

We can run the pilot starting next Tuesday (8/10). We’ll attach the approved IP ranges and an approved IP CSV.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Liu
Head of Security & Privacy, AtlasHealth
samantha@atlashealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: Private deployment discovery — data paths, logging & on‑prem constraints (AtlasHealth)

Looping in a high‑level approach so we can convert this into a one‑page pilot plan:

Option A — VPC PrivateLink (recommended):
- Redwood creates a PrivateLink endpoint service for inference nodes; Atlas creates an ENI in their VPC.
- Egress control: inference nodes only talk to Atlas-approved S3 endpoints + Splunk aggregator inside your VPC.
- KMS: Customer‑managed KMS (Atlas) for persisted artifacts; envelope keys in the Redwood runtime.
- Pros: minimal network footprint, fastest delivery.
- Cons: requires L4‑LB and endpoint acceptance on Atlas side (quick infra work).

Option B — Transit Gateway / TGW attachment:
- Useful if Atlas wants a central route table for many spokes. Slightly more setup but supports scaling across accounts.

Option C — Airgapped on‑prem package (fallback):
- We replicate the runtime artifact bundle; manual artifact updates; no outbound control plane.
- Pros: meets strictest policies.
- Cons: +ops, longer delivery (~6–8 weeks).

Small ops asks to prepare pilot (I can draft):
- Proposed pilot window: 8/10–8/24.
- Pilot scope: 1 instance group, up to 10 rps, Splunk aggregator ingest only, KMS integration, pseudonymization filter applied at agent.
- Deliverables from Redwood: architecture sketch, TF module snippets for PrivateLink, ARO (architecture + runbook), and a short SoW for the pilot.

Aisha — can you take ownership of the ARO? Jordan — can you own the TF snippets? I’ll draft the SoW and price for the 2‑week pilot.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
